editorial:
Imagine moving to a brand new neighborhood where nobody knows you. That's exactly what happens to ten-year-old Laure, a kid who loves football and hates dresses. When a local girl named Lisa assumes Laure is a boy, Laure decides to go along with it and becomes Mickaël. What follows is a warm, sun-soaked summer filled with playground games, new friendships, and first crushes. The movie captures that carefree feeling of childhood summers while quietly building tension about what happens when the truth comes out. It's a gentle, honest story about identity and growing up that feels real from start to finish.

The young lead actor gives a natural, believable performance that carries the whole film. The pacing is slow and relaxed, letting you soak in every moment. On the downside, some viewers might find the ending abrupt and wish for more closure. If you enjoy quiet, character-driven dramas that make you think, this one is for you. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or pick up the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Laure's secret is exposed when her mother forces her to wear a dress and introduces her as a girl to the neighborhood kids. Lisa, who had a crush on Mickaël, feels betrayed and angry. Laure is left isolated and heartbroken, sitting alone in her room. The movie ends without a neat resolution, leaving you to wonder how Laure will navigate her identity going forward. It's a bittersweet conclusion that stays with you long after the credits roll.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quiet coming-of-age stories and character-driven dramas.
